Following preliminary treatment, wastewater is pumped into rectangular primary sedimentation basins to remove floatable and settleable material.
Primary effluent is gravity-fed to 440 acres of mechanically aerated Oxidation Ponds, where organic matter and ammonia are degraded by aerobic and anaerobic bacteria.
Treated pond effluent is pumped to Fixed Growth Reactors (FGRs) (i.e., trickling filters ) that provide additional nitrification of ammonia.

FGR effluent is conveyed to the Dissolved Air Flotation Tanks (DAFTs), where compressed air and polymer are i njected to coagulate, flocculate, and remove biological solids (algae and bacteria) generated during treatment in the Oxidation Ponds and FGRs .
Following biological treatment, the wastewater undergoes filtration through four parallel dual media filters, two of which may be used to produc e recycled water.
Sodium hypochlorite is metered into the filter ed effluent at the beginning of four serpentine chlorine contact tanks to generate a chlorine residual (generally chloramines) for disinfection .
As the effluent leaves the contact tanks , sodium bisulfite is added as needed t o neutralize the hypochlorite.
The Discharger pumps sludge produced in the primary sedimentation basins to primary anaerobic digesters.

Generally, the Discharger operates secondary digester s in series to stabilize and thicken the biosolids prior to dewatering, and to generate biogas used to fuel the plant ’s main influent pump engines and Power Generation Facility.

The Discharger pumps digested sludge (biosolids) to an equalization tank, conditions the biosolids with polymer , and mechanically dewater s them using a belt filter press to approximately 20 to 25 percent solids prior to land application or disposal at a landfill.
